overview: Black answers 1.Nc3 by taking the centre with ...e5, a reversed version of Nimzowitsch's Defence. White normally plays 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.e4 or 2.e4 to reach Vienna and Four Knights structures, with the d4 push possible later. The game is a standard open game with no particular edge for either side, and the root has few games of its own.

white_ideas.idea: Play e4 and Nf3 to reach Vienna/Four Knights set-ups.
Or play g3, Bg2 and d3 for a quiet reversed Sicilian/English feel.

black_ideas.idea: Hold the e5 centre and develop with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6.
Play ...d5 or ...f5 to claim more space.

typical_structures.structure: Open game centre with e4/e5 pawns and symmetrical development.

character.notes: Quiet standard development; no forcing play.

soundness.notes: Sound, though White's edge is small.

structure.notes: Transposes to Vienna/Four Knights; centre in tension.

approach.notes: Masters play 1.Nc3 under one percent of the time; chosen for flexibility and surprise.

level.notes: Transposes to familiar open games; intermediate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Napoleon Attack
sublines_that_differ.how: White opens the centre immediately, a Scotch-like game.

character.reason: Equal open-game play, neither especially solid nor forcing.

structure.reason: Transposes to Vienna and Four Knights centres, with tension.
